newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: No Argentina Brady buyback before Q2 '97 - official.
newsitem.headline: No Argentina Brady buyback before Q2 '97 - official.

text.p: Argentina would be interested in a buyback of Brady bonds but none would be possible until after the first quarter of 1997, said Finance Under Secretary Miguel Kiguel, quoted by Clarin newspaper Tuesday.
Kiguel said that proposals so far presented by banks are not attractive and that there is a danger such an operation could backfire and push up the country's financing costs.

"Basically (the problem) is that we cannot swap the Brady bonds for the same instruments we are using now to finance ourselves in the voluntary credit market. We run the risk of saturating supply and competing with ourselves and that would mean bigger spreads in the new placements," Kiguel told Clarin in London, where he is on an official visit with Economy Minister Roque Fernandez.
But he added, "If an interesting proposal turns up, we could carry out the buyback at any moment."
Asked whether this could happen in 1997, he replied "Our plans for next year are to make big placements in the first quarter to clear the financial horizon. Only after that will be able to decide."
He added "Any other operation can only be considered for second quarter. On January 1 we will start working on next year's program. We will surely start with some placement in marks."

Clarin said that Argentina is planning to end this year's placement program with a $200 million bond in yen, to be presented by Fernandez in a tour of Japan planned for December. The paper did not quote any sources for the information, which came from London.
